args.text: When a process description presents activities as a direct sequence or says one activity happens after another, model the sequence with direct sequence flows rather than adding a gateway unless the description states a decision or parallel paths.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing documented guideline already addresses unnecessary gateways in a described sequence.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Only activities, gateways and events are sequence-flow endpoints. Never connect sequence flows to pools, lanes, data objects, groups or annotations.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.

args.text: When a description states that one activity occurs after another, model the dependency with a direct sequence flow. Do not add a decision gateway for success or failure unless the description states alternative outcomes or a decision.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers the extra testing decision gateway in the generated model.

result.rule: When the description states that a later activity occurs only after an earlier activity succeeds: Model the success outcome as a decision and connect its success path to the dependent activity in the stated order; preserve any other stated outcome paths.

When the description states distinct decisions or approvals at different points in the process: Model each decision or approval at the point stated, and connect it to the activities that precede and follow it in the described order; do not replace one decision with another.
When the description says an activity may take place before a later activity: Model the optional activity as a decision branch with a path that bypasses it; merge the paths before the later activity.

When the description states that named activities may be performed as optional additions to the main sequence: Model each named activity in the optional flow, using gateways to reflect whether the activities are alternatives or whether one or more may occur.

args.text: When a process description states separate assessment activities or criteria, model each distinct activity as a separate BPMN task rather than combining them into one task.

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidance already covers separating distinct activities stated in a description.

result.rule: Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.

result.rule: When When a description names multiple distinct activities within one phase and states that the process continues only after every activity is finished,: model the activities as parallel branches with a parallel split and join, rather than as a sequence.

When the description explicitly lists multiple objectives or criteria that an activity is meant to address: Preserve the stated objectives or criteria in the BPMN task label rather than narrowing the label to only one of them.

When the description names a specific activity and distinguishes it from a related preceding or subsequent activity: Label the BPMN activity with the action stated in the description; do not substitute a related action that the description treats as separate or does not state.

When the description states an activity and provides criteria or other supporting details that are not needed to identify that activity: Label the BPMN element with a concise name for the stated action; omit supporting details that do not distinguish it from another modeled activity, while preserving details that are themselves distinct actions or alternatives.
